data.hypothesis: A portable 64-bit high-bit mask can skip complete ASCII blocks throughout the buffer. For mixed blocks, scalar-decode through the block boundary and any crossing code point, avoiding both repeated per-byte ASCII checks and the prior full bit-plane classifier's boundary bookkeeping. This hybrid may help when complete ASCII blocks occur often; dense mixed-width data may instead pay the mask-check overhead.
data.notes: This is a distinct hybrid experiment, not a full SIMD constraint-mask validator. The earlier T1 bit-plane candidate c557b10fc09a4c93 has overall status runtime_failed; its correctness log records 18 passing cases, but no usable timing is available and the failure cause is not established. Baseline mean was 49.623 microseconds; this candidate has not been measured.
transformations: Retained the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator as validate_utf8_scalar.
Added a portable 64-bit high-bit test, loaded with memcpy, to skip complete ASCII blocks without alignment or endianness assumptions.
For mixed blocks, decoded scalar code points through the block boundary so sequences crossing it are validated once without carried state.
Used the scalar validator for the bounded tail and preserved the run ABI and output.
